payload.text: hv, 10 Nov, FIRST-HAND in vc's session, received by vc's date -u of 13:10Z: "Go with your recommendations." It answered vc's last report, which put four things to hv, and it covers exactly the three vc had made a recommendation on. (1) ST0033's AT-01.2 moves to GREEN without another booking. Its note says precisely what was proven and nothing more: the guard block in engine.bats, extracted by line range and evaluated with fail() stubbed, fires on the zero-arms input it exists for, and on "10 failed" and on a missing summary; the arm itself was seen green in XYJSED and never red in bats; the residual is bats's own run and fail wiring, which XYJSED exercised. That puts the arm on the stateless side of the line this thread drew, where reading suffices, and it is utilz-dc's row to move. (2) THE ORDER OF EDITS TO THE SHARED TEST FILES, because a commit by path takes the whole working-tree file and three changes want arngz.bats: FIRST utilz-dc folds issues 0136 and 0137 into its open change, writing each issue's design before any code as doc-before-code requires, tightens engine.bats's comment that gives the "10 failed" substring as a reason, and lands the lot; THEN vc writes ST0032's AT ids on top of dc's landed files; THEN one full suite run at that head covers all of it, and that run is the cut's own, not an extra one. (3) vc's id fix needs NO fresh mutation run: it is comment-only, and every one of PDY9E2's fourteen mutations targeted the code under test, plan.lua and opt/arngz/arngz, never the test files, so a comment beside an arm cannot change whether that arm reddens. THE FOURTH THING HV'S WORD DOES NOT COVER, because vc gave no recommendation on it and said it would take hv's steer: whether to renumber ST0032's 16 AT rows to unique ids, given that `intent at` has no rename or delete verb and a renumber would strand 16 green rows at the colliding ids. vc's judgement, recorded as vc's and not as hv's, is NOT TO RENUMBER. AT ids follow the work-package numbering by house convention, mirroring the AC ids, so any two threads whose tests share a file will collide by construction; ST0026 and ST0028 avoided it only because ST0026's first work package had no tests. Writing each literal beside its arm with the thread named, as `AT-01.1 (ST0032)`, makes all 16 citations true, including the four that passed the lint falsely on ST0028's and ST0026's literals, and strands nothing. It is also the reversible choice: annotation can still be followed by a renumber, and stranded rows can never be removed. hv can overrule it. The lint's inability to tell one thread's literal from another's is a limit in Intent's tool and not in this contract. STILL OPEN AND HV'S: the head the cut is taken from. Peers read this decision at pickup; dc records no copy.
